 This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 27.01.2016 Passed In Mvc
No.1051/2014 On The File Of The X Additional Judge,
Court Of Small Causes,(Scch-15) Mact, Bangalore,
Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation
And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal Coming On For Hearing This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice T.G. Shivashankare Gowda
 Oral Judgment
The petitioners are seeking enhancement of compensation.

2. For the sake of convenience, rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the
Tribunal.

3.  The brief facts of the case are, on 12.02.2014 at about 05.00 pm while the son of petitioner Nos.1 and 2 and brother of petitioner No.3 by name Sudarshana T, the deceased, walking by the side of the road, opposite to Fouress Company, Peenya, Bangalore City, motor cycle bearing No.KA-04-ER-6201 came from the opposite direction and dashed against the deceased, he sustained injuries and succumbed to death at the hospital.
The NC: 2024:KHC:37472 petitioners seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- have approached the Tribunal.
The claim was opposed by the respondent.
The Tribunal after taking the evidence and hearing both the parties, by impugned judgment and award, assessed the compensation of Rs.10,70,000/- with interest at 9%.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioners are before this Court.
4. Heard the arguments of Sri Rangegowda N.R., learned counsel for the petitioners.
Respondent served and absent.

5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the deceased was 39 years old,
Diploma Holder and he was earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.7,000/- per month and that the compensation awarded under the conventional heads is inadequate and sought for enhancement.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the petitioners and perused the materials on record.
7. The material on record goes to show that there was an accident involving the motorcycle and the deceased on 12.02.2014 at about 5.00 p.m., within the limits of Peenya, Bangalore.
In the accident the deceased sustained the injuries and later died in the hospital.

The prosecution papers such as,

2 FIR, sketch and the charge sheet point out the actionable negligence on the part of the rider-cum-owner of the vehicle.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The rider has faced the trial before the Magistrate.
Hence, the accident is explained, thereby the petitioners being the parents and brother entitled to claim compensation.
8. The petitioners have not produced any evidence in proof of the income.
A person with no proof of income in the year 2014 will be earning not less than Rs.8,500/- per month.
Accordingly, the notional income of the deceased has to be taken.

He was a bachelor at the time of NC:
2024:KHC:37472 accident.
For the age of 39, the applicable multiplier is '15', 40% has to be considered as 'future prospects' and 50% has to be deducted towards 'personal expenses'.

The deceased left behind the parents and brother, hence, towards 'loss of consortium' to parents, 'love and affection' to brother, a sum of Rs.40,000/- each; towards 'funeral expenses' and 'loss of estate' Rs.15,000/- each has to be assessed.

Since the accident is 10 years old, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others 1, 10% appreciation has to be given on 'conventional heads'.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Then the compensation under 'conventional heads' comes to Rs.1,65,000/-.
Total compensation comes to Rs.12,36,000/- as against Rs.10,70,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby, enhancement of Rs.1,66,000/-.
It is the (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC:37472 just compensation that the petitioners are entitled to in the facts and circumstances of the case.
9. The Tribunal awarded interest at 9% per annum on the compensation, since the respondent is not challenging the same, same is kept in tact.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:

ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed-in-part;
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified;
( v) Rest of the judgment and award of the Tribunal is kept intact.

SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE tsn*
